title: bytes_per_token is measured on a dropout-free segmentation, but the frozen contract says it is measured WITH dropout applied -- so SIG's one signature width and DATA's splice gate use a number the training stream never produces.
failure: DATA_AREAS=eng,py, DATA_CORPUS_CAP=200000, TOK_DROPOUT=0.3. Measured: vocab.bytes_per_token = 1.7955 (the deterministic segmentation) while the segmentation the training stream actually consumes yields 1.5639 -- a 12.9% error. Downstream at LM_CTX=128, derive.signature_width_bytes gives 229 bytes instead of 200, so the domain encoder describes 14.5% more material than one loop stride covers, fixed for the lifetime of the run (the exact class of defect signature_width_bytes' own docstring records: "the domain encoder was reading 42% of the material it claimed to describe"). And the verdict of Gate data.splice_window flips: at DATA_SEG_MIN=1500/DATA_SEG_MAX=1900 it prints 'FIRED (7.397 vs 8.0)' on the reported value and 'armed, did not fire (8.492 vs 8.0)' on the value the run actually trains at.
evidence: Line 296 `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` then line 297 measures over those ids (same at line 243 on the replay path). tokenize's docstring, paragraph 2 (lines 391-396), is explicit: "bytes_per_token IS MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED. build_vocabulary measures it over the COUNTING segmentation, which applies tok.dropout, so more and shorter tokens lower it -- and derive.signature_width_bytes(LM.ctx, bytes_per_token) (SIG's one width) and data_plan's splice_window threshold both move with a TOK regularizer."
fix: Measure over a counting segmentation carrying the same dropout as the build passes: `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`, on both the build and replay paths.
_triage_evidence: The BUILD path (tok/api.py:312) now measures with `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)` -- fixed, matching the docstring. Ran it at TOK_DROPOUT=0.3: build-path vocab.bytes_per_token came out 1.9410, matching a fresh dropout-applied measurement (~1.937) and clearly NOT the dropout-free value (2.264). But the REPLAY/resume path (tok/api.py:253) still calls `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` unconditionally. Ran a resume round trip at TOK_DROPOUT=0.3: the resumed vocab.bytes_per_token came out 2.1746, while measuring the SAME sample with dropout actually applied gives 1.8018 -- a ~21% error, reproducing round 1's exact failure mode, but only on the resume branch.
_residue: the resume/replay branch (line 253) still needs `dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream` (vocab.dropout_rng, which is now minted before this point) -- this is exactly the 'fixed on one branch, live on another' pattern the task asked to watch for

title: The RESUME/replay path still measures bytes_per_token dropout-free even though the BUILD path was already fixed to measure it with dropout applied -- SIG's signature width and DATA's splice gate are wrong specifically on every resumed run with TOK_DROPOUT>0, which is goal B's own scenario
failure: The build (online/fixed) arm now correctly measures `bytes_per_token` with dropout applied (line ~309: `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`) -- this fixes round1's finding on that arm. But the replay/resume arm at line 253 still calls `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)`, unchanged. Reproduced end-to-end: built a parent vocabulary online (340 ids, 84 merges) over a repeating sample text, saved its id2bytes sidecar, then resumed with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 via CKPT_RESUME pointing at that sidecar. `build_vocabulary` on the resume returns `bytes_per_token = 16.0` (the dropout-free measurement). Measuring the SAME sample with the SAME vocabulary through the training stream's own dropout (`_segment(child, sample, dropout=0.3, stream=child.dropout_rng)`) gives `bytes_per_token = 11.384` -- a 29% error in the number every resumed run's SIG window width (`derive.signature_width_bytes`) and DATA's splice_window gate are computed from. This is the exact defect round1 filed ("bytes_per_token is measured on a dropout-free segmentation ... SIG's one signature width and DATA's splice gate use a number the training stream never produces"), now live on precisely the branch that matters most for goal B: every run that resumes with regularization on.
evidence: tok/api.py:253 (inside `if read_path:` / `if replayed is not None:`): `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` followed by `vocab.bytes_per_token = _derive.bytes_per_token(len(sample), len(ids))`. Contrast the now-fixed build arm near the function's end: `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)` with the comment "MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED, because the contract says 'the COUNTING segmentation applies tok.dropout' ... A dropout-free measurement describes a segmentation the TRAINING stream never produces." Measured with the repo's own code: parent size 340/merges 84; child (resumed, TOK_DROPOUT=0.3) `build_vocabulary` returns bytes_per_token=16.0; the same vocabulary segmented with dropout=0.3 (what tokenize() actually produces during training) gives bytes_per_token=11.384.
fix: Apply the same fix already applied to the build arm: on the replay branch, measure with `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=vocab.dropout_rng)` instead of `dropout=0.0, stream=None` (the dropout stream is already minted before this line, at what is now line ~244). One measurement rule on both arms, matching the module header's own 'THERE IS NO SECOND ESTIMATOR' claim.

title: The resume/replay branch of build_vocabulary still measures bytes_per_token on a dropout-free segmentation, even though b95c4a4 fixed this exact defect on the build path -- the repair is only half-applied.
failure: CKPT_RESUME set to a real snapshot with TOK_DROPOUT>0 (a resumed continual-learning run, the case this project's numbers are measured across). build_vocabulary's replay branch at line 253 calls `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` unconditionally, ignoring `tok.dropout` and the just-minted `vocab.dropout_rng`, so `vocab.bytes_per_token` on every resume is measured on the deterministic (no-dropout) segmentation -- the exact P1-H16-shaped error the same commit fixed three lines away on the fresh-build path (line 312: `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`). Reproduced end to end: built a vocabulary with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 (bytes_per_token=1.8785, measured with dropout, correct), wrote it out in the `entries` format _replay_merges reads, then resumed by pointing CKPT_RESUME at that file with TOK_DROPOUT=0.3 again. The resumed Vocabulary reports bytes_per_token=2.25 (the dropout-free number) against 1.8801 for a segmentation of the identical text actually drawn with dropout=0.3 from the SAME vocab.dropout_rng the resume branch minted and then never used -- a 19.7% relative error. This number is what SIG's one signature width (derive.signature_width_bytes) and DATA's splice-window gate are computed from on every resumed run, so a resume with dropout on trains with an undersized signature window and an optimistic splice gate, silently, on precisely the run type continual learning is measured across.
evidence: src/tok/api.py:244 mints `vocab.dropout_rng = _rng.rng_for("tok.dropout.mint", seed)` immediately before the replay, but :253 `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` never reads it -- the minted stream is dead on this branch. Compare :312 on the fresh-build path, `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream)`, which b95c4a4 introduced with the comment 'MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED, because the contract says "the COUNTING segmentation applies tok.dropout"... A dropout-free measurement describes a segmentation the TRAINING stream never produces.' Round 1's finding (p4_round1_findings.json, tok/api.py:296) named both sites as one defect ('same at line 243 on the replay path'); the repair's own commit message claims 'bytes_per_token is now measured WITH dropout applied, as the contract states... Identical at the 0.0 default' without qualifying that only one of the two sites changed.
fix: Change line 253 to `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=vocab.dropout_rng)`, mirroring the fresh-build path's fix at line 312.

title: The resume branch measures bytes_per_token with dropout hardcoded to 0.0, ignoring TOK_DROPOUT
failure: On the parent-replay path (`read_path` set), bytes_per_token is measured via `_segment(vocab, sample, dropout=0.0, stream=None)` (line 253) -- dropout is a literal 0.0 regardless of what `tok.dropout` is set to. The fresh-build path a few lines later (line 312) correctly measures with `dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=stream`, and the docstring explicitly requires the dropout-applied measurement ('MEASURED WITH DROPOUT APPLIED, because the contract says "the COUNTING segmentation applies tok.dropout" ... A dropout-free measurement describes a segmentation the TRAINING stream never produces'). So every resumed run with TOK_DROPOUT>0 computes a bytes_per_token that the resumed run's own training stream will never actually produce, and that wrong number feeds directly into SIG's signature width (derive.signature_width_bytes) and DATA's data_plan splice_window gate threshold.
evidence:
Reproduced live: built a fresh vocabulary (TOK_DROPOUT=0), wrote it out in the `entries` format _replay_merges expects, pointed CKPT_RESUME at it, then rebuilt with TOK_DROPOUT=0.5 so build_vocabulary took the resume/replay branch.
  resumed vocab.bytes_per_token (as actually produced) = 1.8613551037426268
  bytes_per_token measured on the SAME sample with dropout=0.5 applied (what the contract requires) = 1.4357707935505175
The resumed value is identical to the dropout=0 value and about 30% off from what the contract specifies. This is a distinct, still-live bug from round1's tok/api.py:296 finding -- that finding was about the general/build measurement, which has since been fixed on the fresh-build arm (line 312 now correctly applies dropout); the fix was never extended to the resume/replay branch, the same 'fixed on one branch, missed on the other' pattern already recorded twice in this file's comments (tok.dropout.mint minting, and the fixed-arm ceiling close).
fix: Change line 253 to `ids, _pos = _segment(vocab, sample, dropout=float(tok.dropout), stream=vocab.dropout_rng if float(tok.dropout) > 0 else None)`, mirroring the fresh-build path, so a resumed dropout>0 run measures bytes_per_token the same way a fresh one does.

title: tokenize performs a re-segmentation whose match table has not moved, instead of refusing it and counting tok.retok_noop
failure: The documented refusal and its (size, len(seq2id)) invariant stamp are entirely absent from the body. Ran it: two consecutive `tokenize` calls on the same bytes with an unchanged vocabulary both run in full and both return 500 ids -- no stamp, no refusal, no counter. The docstring puts a price on this: "the rebuild is byte-identical but the side effects are not, and the measured cost of not refusing was 2.189 b/B and 68 points of word quality (23 retoks, 22 adding zero tokens)". Nothing distinguishes a real retokenization from a no-op one in any artifact.
evidence: Docstring: "A RE-SEGMENTATION WHOSE MATCH TABLE HAS NOT MOVED since the last one is REFUSED here and counted as tok.retok_noop, not performed ... The invariant stamped is (size, len(seq2id)) and NOT size alone, because retire() changes the match table without changing vocab_size." The body (lines 405-431) computes `drop`, picks the stream, calls `_segment`, maps labels and returns.
fix: Stamp (vocab.size(), len(vocab.seq2id)) on the Vocabulary at each segmentation; on a call whose stamp is unchanged return the previous Segmentation and increment tok.retok_noop, with the skip test disabled whenever dropout > 0 as the docstring specifies.
_triage_evidence: tokenize()'s body (tok/api.py:462-488) is unchanged: no stamp is taken, no comparison against a previous (size, len(seq2id)) pair, and no tok.retok_noop counter exists anywhere. Vocabulary.__slots__ (lines 74-76) still carries no stamp field. `grep -n retok_noop src/tok/api.py` finds it only in docstring prose.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area

title: the replay path neither reconciles the file's recorded settings nor distinguishes an unreadable parent vocabulary from a cold start
failure: `_replay_merges` reads only `blob["id2bytes"]` and drops every other key, so a resume launched with TOK_MIN_PAIR=200 against a parent built at 50 runs on the parent's table and prints nothing -- ISSUES P1-M80/L20 exactly, which the docstring cites as the thing this arm exists to fix. Separately, `_replay_merges` returns None when the file is missing and the body falls straight through to a fresh build: ran it with d_vocab_read_path="/nonexistent/parent.dyntok.json" and got a freshly minted 340-token vocabulary and no refusal, so the restored embedding table is indexed by a different vocabulary -- the failure the same paragraph says MUST NOT happen -- while CKPT.load raises loudly for the analogous missing checkpoint.
evidence: Docstring: "The file's recorded vmax/min_pair/max_tok/dropout DO NOT WIN: this package holds one declaration, the levers, and any disagreement is printed as a reconciliation line and counted" and "a resume MUST reuse the saved vocabulary or the restored embedding table is indexed by a different vocabulary". DID IT FIRE names `tok.load_reconciled`. Body: `replayed = _replay_merges(vocab, read_path); if replayed is not None: ...` with no else branch.
fix: Compare blob['min_pair'|'max_bytes'|'dropout'|'vmax'] against the resolved levers and emit one reconciliation line per disagreement with a tok.load_reconciled count; and raise when read_path is non-empty but unreadable, naming the path, instead of silently building a new vocabulary.
_triage_evidence: No reconciliation of the file's vmax/min_pair/max_tok/dropout against the resolved levers exists anywhere in build_vocabulary or _replay_merges -- confirmed by reading both functions in full; there is no tok.load_reconciled counter or comparison code. For the 'unreadable parent' half: ran build_vocabulary with CKPT_RESUME pointing at a path whose .dyntok.json does not exist -- it no longer silently falls through to a fresh build (round 1's exact repro); instead it now RAISES RngError('tok.dropout.mint was already issued for seed 0') from inside build_vocabulary itself, because the unconditional mint added at line 244 (for the dropout_rng fix) is minted a second time at line 270 when `_replay_merges` returns None and execution falls through past the early-return block.
_residue: the specific silent-fresh-build repro round 1 measured no longer occurs verbatim (it crashes instead of silently succeeding), but neither half of what the finding asks for -- reconciliation, or a clear NAMED refusal distinguishing an unreadable parent from a cold start -- exists; the current behavior is an unrelated, confusing RngError rather than either the old silent success or the requested clear refusal, which is arguably a regression introduced by the partial dropout_rng fix

title: the declared Gate tok.build_passes_advice is never produced on any arm, so mode="fixed" runs silently at 2 passes where the build of record used 8
failure: The contract makes this a three-state gate that is never silent: on mode="fixed" it must print `build_passes=2; the offline build historically used 8 -- set TOK_BUILD_PASSES=8 to reproduce it`, and on the other two arms `unreachable (mode != fixed)`. The body creates no Gate at all -- tok/api.py does not even import spine.gate -- and there is no TOK counters() entry point and no counters/gates slot on Vocabulary, so there is no channel for it. An operator running mode="fixed" at the default build_passes=2 gets no statement that this is not the offline build of record, which the docstring flags as belonging on P9's list of numbers that moved.
evidence: Docstring: "The 8 is not lost: it is a DECLARED GATE with its predicate, tok.build_passes_advice ... Advice that appears sometimes and says nothing when it does not is armed-but-inert applied to prose." Imports at the head of tok/api.py: `from spine import derive as _derive` and `from spine import rng as _rng` -- no `Gate`. The same absence kills the other named surfaces here (tok.build_pass, tok.build_mint, tok.build_converged, tok.load_reconciled).
fix: Import spine.gate, carry a `gates`/`counters` slot on Vocabulary (or add TOK.counters), and emit Gate("tok.build_passes_advice", fired=(mode=="fixed"), value=build_passes, threshold=8, reachable=(mode=="fixed"), reason="mode != fixed").
_triage_evidence: tok/api.py has no `from spine import gate` / `from spine.gate import Gate` import (confirmed: only collections, dataclasses, spine.lever.Config, spine.derive, spine.rng are imported), no Gate(...) call anywhere in the file, and Vocabulary.__slots__ has no counters/gates field to carry one on. `grep -n build_passes_advice src/tok/api.py` finds it only in docstring prose.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area

title: The re-segmentation no-op refusal is absent: no invariant is stamped, so a re-tokenization whose match table has not moved is performed rather than refused, and tok.retok_noop can never be counted.
failure: tokenize is the single entry point for the initial segmentation, every in-loop re-segmentation, the final one and the held-out encode, and it holds no state whatsoever about the previous call. Calling it twice with an unchanged vocabulary performs the full segmentation again and returns a fresh Segmentation both times, with no way for any caller or report to tell a real retokenization from a no-op. The measured cost of not refusing is stated in the contract as 2.189 b/B and 68 points of word quality over 23 retoks of which 22 added zero tokens; that cost is fully reintroduced, and the three-state DID IT FIRE row tok.retok / tok.retok_noop collapses to one.
evidence: Lines 404-430 are the whole body: read dropout, pick the stream, `_segment`, map labels, return. The docstring at lines 365-369 requires the opposite: "A RE-SEGMENTATION WHOSE MATCH TABLE HAS NOT MOVED since the last one is REFUSED here and counted as tok.retok_noop, not performed ... The invariant stamped is (size, len(seq2id)) and NOT size alone, because retire() changes the match table without changing vocab_size." `Vocabulary.__slots__` (lines 74-76) carries no slot for the stamp, so P4 did not build the surface either.
fix: Add a stamp slot to Vocabulary, record (vocab.size(), len(vocab.seq2id)) on each segmentation, and when a caller asks for a re-segmentation at an unchanged stamp, return the previous Segmentation and count tok.retok_noop -- disabling the test whenever drop > 0, as the docstring requires.
_triage_evidence: Duplicate of the earlier retok_noop finding; same unchanged tokenize() body, same absence of a stamp field on Vocabulary.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area

title: The saved file's recorded settings are never read, so the documented reconciliation (tok.load_reconciled) and the tok.build_passes_advice Gate are mechanisms that cannot fire.
failure: A resume that sets TOK_MIN_PAIR=200 against a parent saved at min_pair=50 -- the case the docstring cites by id -- produces no reconciliation line, no counter and no difference in behaviour: the body reads nothing from the file except id2bytes, so the divergence between this run's declaration and the parent's recorded fact is invisible in exactly the way P1-M80/P1-L20 record ("the audit then printed 'NOTHING READ THESE' naming a knob that was set and ignored"). Likewise a TOK_MODE=fixed run at the default TOK_BUILD_PASSES=2 prints nothing saying it is not the offline build of record, because the Gate that was supposed to carry the retired literal 8 does not exist -- spine.gate is not even imported in this module and Vocabulary has no field to hang it on, so the Q-TOK-9 ruling's replacement for the number is silence.
evidence: Line 309 reads only `blob.get("id2bytes", ...)`; `vmax`, `min_pair`, `max_tok`, `dropout` are never touched, against the docstring at lines 160-164 ("The file's recorded vmax/min_pair/max_tok/dropout DO NOT WIN ... any disagreement is printed as a reconciliation line and counted") and lines 200-203 ("DID IT FIRE: ... tok.load_reconciled, Gate tok.build_passes_advice (fires on mode=\"fixed\" with the two numbers; 'unreachable (mode != fixed)' otherwise -- never silence)"). `grep Gate src/tok/api.py` finds only docstring text.

_triage_evidence: Duplicate of the reconciliation half of the earlier 'replay path neither reconciles...' finding, plus the Gate absence confirmed above (no spine.gate import, no Gate calls in tok/api.py). _replay_merges (lines 317-369) reads only `entries`/`id2bytes` and `pair`; it never reads or compares vmax/min_pair/max_tok/dropout from the blob.
_residue: exact reproduction of round 1's finding -- no code change in this area

title: The re-segmentation no-op refusal the docstring specifies does not exist in the body
failure: tokenize's docstring (lines 423-427) specifies: 'A RE-SEGMENTATION WHOSE MATCH TABLE HAS NOT MOVED since the last one is REFUSED here and counted as tok.retok_noop, not performed ... The invariant stamped is (size, len(seq2id)) and NOT size alone.' The actual body (lines 462-488) has no state to compare against a previous call, no stamped invariant, and no refusal path -- it unconditionally calls `_segment` on every invocation regardless of whether the vocabulary's match table moved since the last call. tok.retok_noop, one of the function's declared DID IT FIRE rows, can therefore never be counted because nothing in this function ever computes or checks the condition that would increment it.
evidence: Read tokenize's full body (lines 462-488): the only state read is `tok.mode`, `tok.dropout`, and `vocab`'s live fields for segmentation itself; there is no comparison of `(vocab.size(), len(vocab.seq2id))` against any prior value, no cache, no early return. Still live -- identical to round1's tok/api.py:405/420 findings, and the docstring's own measured cost figures ('2.189 b/B and 68 points of word quality (23 retoks, 22 adding zero tokens)') describe exactly the failure mode this missing check would prevent.
fix: Track `(vocab.size(), len(vocab.seq2id))` from the previous tokenize() call that had regularize=False/represented a real re-tokenization (module-level or Vocabulary-attached state), compare it at entry, and short-circuit with a tok.retok_noop count instead of calling _segment when the invariant is unchanged.

title: build_vocabulary declares cand_window, mint_pmin and mint_novel as LEVERS READ and reads none of them, so three knobs are inert during the build with the audit reporting them as read
failure: TOK_MINT_NOVEL=1 (or TOK_MINT_PMIN=0.2, or TOK_CAND_WINDOW=64) with TOK_MODE=fixed or online. The build loop at :262-276 selects purely by `tally.most_common()` and `tok.min_pair`; there is no candidate window, no novelty re-sort and no conditional-probability floor. The resulting vocabulary is byte-identical to the run with those knobs unset, while the declared LEVERS READ line says this entry point consumed them. That is the ISSUES P1-M80/L20 shape the same docstring cites ('the audit then printed "NOTHING READ THESE" naming a knob that was set and ignored'), and it widens the computed affects() set the L3 isolation sweep is read against, so a real coupling through those levers would be pre-declared and invisible.
evidence: :197-198 `LEVERS READ: mode, seed_vocab, build_passes, build_bytes, min_pair, max_bytes, cand_window, mint_pmin, mint_novel, dropout`. `grep -n 'cand_window\|mint_pmin\|mint_novel' src/tok/api.py` finds them only in prose and in mint_burst's own LEVERS READ line at :533 -- mint_burst is still a stub, so nothing in the tree reads them.
fix: Either implement the selection rules in the build pass (the docstring at :511-523 spells them out: materialize cand_window candidates floored at 2, re-sort by novelty when mint_novel > 0, skip candidates whose p(b|a) is below mint_pmin) or remove the three names from build_vocabulary's LEVERS READ line and leave them declared on mint_burst alone.
_triage_evidence: tok/api.py:197-198 still lists cand_window, mint_pmin, mint_novel in LEVERS READ. `grep -n 'cand_window|mint_pmin|mint_novel' src/tok/api.py` (restricted to build_vocabulary's body, lines 208-314) finds none; they appear only in mint_burst's docstring, and mint_burst is still a stub (raises NotImplementedError).
_residue: mint_burst, where these levers actually belong, is a still-in-progress stub, per the task's own instruction not to flag stub entry points -- but the finding is specifically about build_vocabulary's LEVERS READ line, which is not a stub and is unchanged

title: The fixed arm overwrites Vocabulary.ceiling, the field the package header declares comes from the wire on every path, with the achieved build size
failure: TOK_MODE=fixed with LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=4096 and a build that reaches 512. After :290, vocab.ceiling is 512 while the model's embedding and head still have 4096 rows. Every later reader of vocab.ceiling as 'the model's embedding row count' -- the banner, vocab_state's recorded vmax, LM.mint_rows' bound, and the D-T1 reconciliation that compares a saved file's vmax against the wire -- now reads a number DATA/TOK computed rather than the one LM.vocab_slots supplies, and a resume's reconciliation is taken against a package-mutated value. The intended effect (never mint again) is already available through soft_cap without touching the wire-sourced field.
evidence: :290 `vocab.ceiling = vocab.size()`. Module header :14-16: 'The ceiling is HARD AND COMES FROM THE WIRE ON EVERY PATH, INCLUDING A RESUME; the `vmax` inside a saved tokenizer file is a recorded fact to reconcile against, never an authority (DEFECT D-T1...)'. Class docstring :63-67: '`ceiling` is HARD and arrives as the wire d_vocab_ceiling from LM.vocab_slots -- it is the model's embedding row count'.
fix: Add a third, TOK-owned field (e.g. `closed_at`) that at_cap()/_cap() also min()s over, and leave `ceiling` holding the wire value for the life of the run. That gives the fixed arm its hard stop without making the recorded ceiling disagree with LM.vocab_slots, which is what P1-H57's repair was reaching for when it moved the write off soft_cap.
_triage_evidence: tok/api.py:300 still does `vocab.ceiling = vocab.size()` on the build path (and, newly, also at :252 on the replay path -- see the separate 'closes only on the build path' finding, now fixed for that specific inconsistency). The module header (lines 15-19) and the Vocabulary class docstring (lines 67-71) are unchanged and still say unconditionally that ceiling 'is HARD and arrives as the wire d_vocab_ceiling from LM.vocab_slots -- it is the model's embedding row count.' Ran it: build a mode=fixed vocabulary against LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=4096 that reaches only 512 tokens -- vocab.ceiling reads 512, not 4096.
_residue: a long defending paragraph was added inside build_vocabulary's own docstring (lines 289-300) arguing this narrowing is safe because it can only ever shrink the cap and the model keeps its spare rows -- but the class- and module-level docstrings that state ceiling always equals the wire value were not updated to carve out this exception, so the contract is now internally inconsistent rather than resolved, and round 1's suggested fix (a separate closed_at field) was not adopted

title: build_vocabulary's LEVERS READ declares cand_window, mint_pmin and mint_novel; the function body never reads any of them
